summary: Implement a minimal stateless Node.js 22 HTTP health service using only the built-in http and node:test modules. The service exposes GET /health (200, {"status":"ok"}), returns 404 JSON for unknown routes while remaining healthy, and separates an exported server factory from a startup entry point that listens on process.env.PORT (default 3000). Tests exercise real HTTP behavior on an ephemeral loopback port. No database, Docker, identity provider, third-party packages, or cloud infrastructure is required.

tasks.description: Create the exported HTTP server factory module (app.cjs) that constructs a Node http.Server handling GET /health (200 JSON {"status":"ok"}) and all other routes (404 JSON error), without calling listen().

contracts.description: Exported factory createServer() returns an un-started node:http.Server; the caller owns listen/close.
GET /health responds 200 with JSON body exactly {"status":"ok"}.
Any path other than /health responds 404 with a JSON error body; service remains able to serve /health afterward.

tasks.description: Create the executable startup entry (server.cjs) that imports the factory, parses process.env.PORT (default 3000), and listens, keeping the process alive.

contracts.description: npm start listens on process.env.PORT with a default of 3000 and does not close the listener.
Startup entry and application factory are separate files so tests never spawn a fixed-port server.

tasks.description: Write real HTTP tests using node:test that start the factory on loopback port 0, assert /health, an unknown route, and /health again, then close the server.

contracts.description: npm test performs actual HTTP requests (no mocks) against an ephemeral loopback port and closes the server in teardown.

tasks.description: Create package.json with pinned (empty) dependency set, start/test/build scripts, and CommonJS (.cjs) conformance.

contracts.description: npm test runs node --test test/app.test.cjs; npm run build runs node --check over all source files; npm start runs node src/server.cjs.
No runtime or development dependencies are declared; only Node built-ins are used.

tasks.description: Add a portability-safe build script helper that runs node --check across all .cjs source files (plain npm script invoking node --check per file).

contracts.description: npm run build verifies JavaScript syntax of all source files; implementation defined as an assumption: uses node --check invoked from a helper script.

tasks.description: Write README.md with install/start/test/build instructions and a source-to-requirement mapping.

contracts.description: README documents install/start/test instructions and maps each source file to FR/NFR requirements.

assumptions: npm run build is implemented as a helper script (scripts/check-syntax.cjs) that invokes node --check on src/app.cjs and src/server.cjs; the original document only states that build 'checks all source JavaScript syntax' without specifying a mechanism.
The JSON error body for unknown routes is {"error":"Not Found"} with a 404 status; the document specifies 'a JSON error' without a fixed shape.
Only named start/test/build scripts are required; no lockfile is authored by the model (host generates npm lockfiles during install).
The /health response Content-Type is application/json; the document specifies only the status code and JSON body.
The startup entry does not add explicit signal handlers; the default process termination behavior is acceptable given the document does not require graceful shutdown of the startup process.
conflicts: None. The two input documents are consistent: the architecture view mirrors FR3's factory/startup separation and NFR1's ephemeral-port testing.

verification.unit: npm test runs node --test against test/app.test.cjs with no live database, Redis, or identity provider.
verification.build: npm run build runs node --check over all source files.
verification.startup: npm start keeps an HTTP listener alive on process.env.PORT and answers GET /health.

host_validation.limitation: Checks structural references, not semantic coverage or interface compatibility
